chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from his father Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Abdillah, from 'Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from 'Abdillah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'What is the reward for one who visits the grave of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), as a visitor, knowing his right, neither reluctant nor arrogant?' He said, 'One thousand accepted Hajj and one thousand purified 'Umrah are recorded for him. And if he was wretched, he is recorded as blissful, and he will continuously be submerged in the Mercy of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) with humility and knowledge?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh highlights the transformative power of Ziyarat al-Husayn, where the visitor's status is elevated from wretched to blissful through divine mercy. This tradition underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory and expiatory efficacy of visiting the Imam's grave, linking physical pilgrimage to spiritual redemption. The emphasis on 'knowing his right' (bi-haqqihi) reflects the scholarly focus on proper reverence and theological understanding during the visit.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from his father Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā ibn ‘Abdillāh, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Mughīrah, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Maymūn Al-Qaddāḥ, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “What is the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) while knowing his rights and without any pride or arrogance?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “One thousand accepted Hajj and one thousand purified ‘Umrah will be registered for them. And (even) if they are among the wretched ones, they will be registered among the blissful ones and they will be continuously submerged in the Mercy of Allāh.”
